about: Yearly events the blog writes one lasting article for. One input to the daily job's choice of question (INSTRUCTIONS.md, step 1): an event wins on the first day it is due, and the normal source of questions wins on every other day. 'publish_from' is the first day the article may be published. It is never the date of the event. 'event_date' is when the thing itself happens, with the source it was checked against on 16 Nov 2026; the job confirms it again before writing. Each id is used as the opp_id when publishing, so covered.json records it and it is written once. Approved by Garry on 16 Nov 2026. Edited only by the planning chat (Fable).

events.event: The energy price cap changes each quarter
events.event_date: The cap changes on 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October. It does NOT change on 1 December. Ofgem announces each new level about five weeks earlier: 25 November 2026 for 1 January to 31 March 2027, then 23 February 2027 and 26 May 2027 for the next two quarters.
events.event_date_checked: Ofgem news: 'Changes to energy price cap between 1 October and 31 December 2026' (lists the next announcement dates)
events.question: The energy price cap is changing. What does that mean for my bill?

events.event: Mother's Day in the UK (Mothering Sunday)
events.event_date: Sunday 7 March 2027. It is the fourth Sunday of Lent, three weeks before Easter, so it moves each year (26 March in 2028). The US date in May is a different day.

events.event: Council tax bills for the new year
events.event_date: Councils send the yearly bill during March, for the year that starts on 1 April. Timing varies by council.
